environment.api: FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8012, developer PostGIS container ratsight-full-local-postgres-1 at 127.0.0.1:54330
environment.basemap: external positron style stubbed with an empty style document; application layers unaffected

scenario.flow: zoom to a bounded viewport, select the nearest published sighting cell, run the default simulation, switch to individual trajectories, advance four steps, then drag the map for 3.2 s

before.description: HEAD MapView with the map-anchored popup and a full remove/re-add of simulation sources and layers on every preview and playback change

after.description: Current MapView with stable sources/layers, a single preview cache, and GSAP reveal/flow/walker animation

comparison.preview_latency_ms: +1.8% (57 ms; backend-dominated, not a regression claim)
comparison.heap_post_gc_with_simulation_mb: +1.6 MB with animated sources (no memory-regression claim)

interpretation: Map panning was already frame-locked before this change; the measured rendering win is the removal of source and layer reconstruction during preview and playback, not a higher pan frame rate.
Playback now updates existing sources through setData instead of rebuilding layers; four steps cost 8 setData calls and zero builds/source rebuilds.
The reveal animation is new behaviour and therefore has no before value; it ran at about 65 frames per second on this machine.

Preview latency and payload size are unchanged because they are dominated by the simulation response (about 1.9 MB of trajectories plus network geometry), which this frontend-only change does not alter.
limitations: One machine, one headless Chromium build, one selected cell, and the default 24 walkers / 12 steps; not a capacity benchmark.
Development servers, not a production build or CDN.
No Safari, Firefox, or low-end hardware measurements.
The baseline had no GeoJSON-duration instrumentation, so geographic processing is evidenced by eliminated rebuilds rather than an isolated duration.
Geojson build duration and animation frame-time distribution are sampled from the data-map-perf telemetry, not a full Chrome trace.
The 3.2 s scripted drag covers pan with a simulation visible; zoom gestures and mobile drag performance were not measured.
